description: Cooking techniques for the converter, derived from the de-DE MC Smart corpus. Numbers and generic phrases only, in our own words; no recipe text.

fields.device.mode: Recommended mode for an uploaded draft. Official practice that differs is listed under alternatives and notes.
fields.device.temperature: °C; typical = median, range = [p10, p90] of the basis group in the recommended mode (nearest rank, so every value is one the device used).
fields.device.timeSeconds: Seconds; typical = median, range = [p10, p90]. formula, when present, is an expression in massGrams (bowl content), flourGrams or temperature, using tMinSeconds() from timing-model.json; clamp(lo, hi, x) limits x to [lo, hi]. formulaR2 is the R² of a fitted formula; the converter's prompt leaves out formulas below 0.3.
fields.device.speed: typical = median, max = p90 of the basis group, capped by the rules in device-limits.json (3 when heated or in reverse, 4 with the whisk). null for program modes, which store no speed.
fields.device.reverse: true, false, or a condition the converter decides per recipe.
fields.device.accessory.measuringCup: in, out, either (the recipe decides) or n/a.
fields.device.accessory.attachment: null, whisk (Rühraufsatz), cooking_basket (Kocheinsatz in the bowl), cooking_basket_on_lid (Kocheinsatz as splash guard), steamer (Dampfgaraufsatz), food_processor.
fields.alternatives: Other modes the corpus uses for the same technique, with their own quantiles; included when they cover at least 10 % of the technique's steps or carry a note.
fields.evidence.statsMode: Mode whose steps supplied the device numbers. It differs from device.mode when official recipes use a mode that the member editor does not offer (kneading); recommendedModeObserved then shows the numbers of the recommended mode.
fields.evidence.basis: official when the recommended mode has at least 20 official steps for this technique, otherwise all recipes.
fields.evidence.selection: How steps were assigned to the technique. Technique labels come from a rule-based classifier that was about 85-90 % correct on a manual spot check of about 100 steps.
fields.ingredientClasses: vegetables, onion_garlic, herbs, nuts_seeds, hard_cheese, chocolate, fruit, meat, fish, dairy, egg, flour_dough, sugar_spices, bread_biscuits, rice_grain, pasta, potatoes, liquid, ice

techniques.label: Weigh an ingredient into the bowl with the built-in scale
structure: One scale step per ingredient added by weight; the title starts with amount and name, for example "200 g Wasser" (78.7 % of official scale titles start with "<N> g").
74.3 % of scale steps weigh exactly the gram amount of the one ingredient they name; split an ingredient across two scale steps only when it goes in at two points of the recipe.
The text step right before a scale step names the same ingredient in only 3.2 % of cases: it prepares something else (cutting, fitting an accessory).
Amounts below 5 g never go on the scale; write them in a text step in Tl, Prise or Msp.
notes: Scale steps carry text on the device, like turbo steps; all other program steps show only their title.

techniques.label: Chop onions, shallots, garlic or ginger

alternatives.note: Turbo for 2 s (1-5 s) is an equal choice before sautéing: official recipes chop onion or garlic with turbo in about a third of cases (98 of 290 chops before the first heated step). Turbo needs contents at room temperature, no whisk and at most 2500 g in the bowl.

structure: Text step before: peel and halve the onions (peeling is named in 35 % of the text before official chopping steps, halving in 20 %); garlic cloves go in whole.
Measuring cup in the lid (state at cold manual steps: inserted 724, removed 237).
Text step after the step: "mit dem Spatel nach unten schieben" when the next step works on the same contents (75.7 % of these phrases follow cold chopping, 18.6 % turbo).
Usually followed by fat in a scale step and the sauté or roasting step.

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names onion, shallot, garlic or ginger

techniques.label: Chop vegetables coarse or fine
structure: Text step before: peel and cut into pieces (pieces are named in 18 %, quartering in 14 % of the text before official chopping steps).
Speed 5 chops coarse, 6-8 fine; for a finer result run a second short step instead of a longer one.
Measuring cup in the lid (state at cold manual steps: inserted 724, removed 237).
Text step after the step: "mit dem Spatel nach unten schieben" when the next step works on the same contents (75.7 % of these phrases follow cold chopping, 18.6 % turbo).

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names a vegetable

techniques.label: Chop fresh herbs
structure: Text step before: pick the leaves from the stems; the ingredient list counts herbs as Stück of stems (Petersilienstiele, Thymianstiele).
Chop herbs while the bowl is still dry, then transfer and set them aside when they are used at the end.

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names a herb

techniques.label: Chop nuts or seeds
structure: For ground nuts use grind_fine (speed 8-10, 10-20 s) instead.
Measuring cup in the lid (state at cold manual steps: inserted 724, removed 237).

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names nuts, almonds or seeds

techniques.label: Grate hard cheese
structure: Text step before: cut the cheese into pieces; grate it first in the dry bowl and set it aside when the recipe needs it later.
Measuring cup in the lid (state at cold manual steps: inserted 724, removed 237).

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names cheese

techniques.label: Chop chocolate or couverture
structure: Text step before: break the chocolate into pieces.
Chop before melting; the melt step follows in the same bowl at about 50 °C.

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names chocolate or couverture

techniques.label: Chop fruit
structure: Text step before: peel, core and cut into pieces.
Measuring cup in the lid (state at cold manual steps: inserted 724, removed 237).

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names a fruit

techniques.label: Chop or mince meat, ham or fish
structure: Text step before: cut into pieces of about 3 cm; the meat should be well chilled.

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names meat, ham, bacon or fish

techniques.label: Make crumbs from bread, rolls or biscuits
structure: Text step before: break into pieces; bread from the day before.

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 5-10, at most 15 s, text since the previous machine step names bread, rolls, rusks or biscuits

techniques.label: Turbo pulse for coarse chopping
structure: Turbo is its own step; its title names the seconds ("Turbo-Taste für 2 Sekunden"); the number matches the programmed time in 99.6 % of 262 such titles.
Turbo steps sit early in the recipe (68 % in the first third) and are often followed by roasting (83 times).
Never with the whisk fitted; never on hot contents (SmartRecipe rule: at most 60 °C) and at most 2500 g in the bowl.
Text step after the step: "mit dem Spatel nach unten schieben" when the next step works on the same contents (75.7 % of these phrases follow cold chopping, 18.6 % turbo).
notes: Official recipes use 2 s most (125 of 244 steps); all sources together have median 3 s.

techniques.label: Grind fine: sugar to icing sugar, grains, spices, ground nuts
structure: The bowl must be completely dry.
Measuring cup in; let the dust settle before opening the lid.

techniques.label: Crush ice or blend frozen fruit (sorbet, ice cream)
structure: Frozen fruit straight from the freezer; push down with the spatula and repeat a short step if lumps remain.

techniques.label: Stir or mix cold ingredients
structure: Text step before: name everything that goes in ("zugeben", "in den Mixbehälter geben").
Speed 4 is the mixing speed (median 30 s at speed 4); speed 2-3 for short stirs.

techniques.label: Fold in or stir gently so pieces stay whole (reverse rotation)
structure: Reverse rotation makes the blade stir instead of cut (official guide); use it whenever solid pieces must stay whole.
Speed with reverse never above 3.

techniques.label: Blend smooth (cold purée, pesto, dip, dressing)

alternatives.note: The puree program (30-60 s) does the same job; member recipes use it, official recipes almost never (3 steps).

structure: Text step before: name what goes in; liquids first for a smoother result.
Push down with the spatula and repeat a short step instead of one long one.

evidence.selection: manual mode, 0 °C, speed 8-10, at least 20 s (how official recipes purée cold contents)

techniques.label: Purée a hot soup or sauce after cooking

timeSeconds.formulaNote: puree program time vs bowl mass, R² 0.13 (n 76): the time is nearly fixed at 30-60 s

structure: Measuring cup in before puréeing hot contents (at ramp steps the cup was inserted 30 times, never removed).

Never start hot contents at a high speed. Without the puree program, use manual steps at 0 °C with rising speed, starting at speed 4 or lower, for example 10 s each at speed 4, 6 and 8 (official ramps run 4>5>6>7>8 at about 10 s per phase).
Purée is the last machine step of a soup (63 % of ramp steps sit in the last third of the recipe).
notes: Official recipes purée hot soup with the ramp mode (35 of 52 official steps); member recipes use the puree program. The member editor offers the puree program but not ramp on MC3.0; the server stores ramp from a member account, but whether the device plays it is untested.

techniques.label: Blend a drink or smoothie
structure: Text step before: solids first, liquid on top; with turbo at most 2500 g in the bowl (SmartRecipe rule).

techniques.label: Whip cream, egg whites or eggs with sugar (whisk attachment)
structure: Own text step to fit the whisk attachment ("Rühraufsatz einsetzen", 230 text steps) and one to remove it afterwards (125).
With the whisk fitted the speed is at most 4 (official guide; 92 % of steps with the whisk run at speed 4 or lower).
Bowl and whisk must be free of fat for egg whites; cream should be cold.
Whipping time depends on fat content and temperature, so the text step after says to check the stiffness.

techniques.label: Emulsify: mayonnaise, aioli, creamy dressings
structure: The oil is poured slowly onto the lid while the measuring cup stays in, so it runs in along the cup in a thin stream ("das Öl langsam auf den Deckel gießen, sodass es am Messbecher entlang in den Mixbehälter läuft"); 16 of 17 official oil emulsions pour the oil onto the lid, none through the lid opening.
Two-step pattern: a short step (about 10 s) mixes the base, then a long step at speed 4 (top setting 240 s, 13 of 17 official oil emulsions) runs while the oil is poured onto the lid.

techniques.label: Mix a cake batter or sponge mixture
structure: Soft butter, eggs at room temperature; add the flour last and mix only until combined.
Push down with the spatula between two short mixing steps.

techniques.label: Dissolve yeast in lukewarm liquid
structure: Text step before: crumble the fresh yeast into the liquid with a little sugar.
Yeast never above 37 °C (SmartRecipe rule); 37 °C for 180 s at speed 1 is the standard setting (53 of 84 official steps).
Followed directly by the flour and the kneading step (83 transitions from warm/dissolve to knead).

techniques.label: Knead a yeast dough

timeSeconds.formulaNote: kneading time vs flour in the bowl, R² 0.10: the time is a plateau at 120 s up to 1250 g flour

recommendedModeObserved.note: device numbers above come from the kneading mode; this is what recipes using kneading_solid_dough programmed

structure: At most 1000 g flour per kneading step (corpus maximum 1000 g, p90 600 g; SmartRecipe rule 1000 g).
Text step after: let the dough rise covered outside the machine and name the time (52 % of recipes name passive time in text).
notes: Official recipes use the kneading program (120 s in 79 of 115 official yeast-dough steps); member recipes use kneading_solid_dough. The member editor offers only the kneading_*_dough variants on MC3.0; the server stores kneading from a member account, but whether the device plays it is untested.

techniques.label: Mix a short crust or another firm dough without yeast

recommendedModeObserved.note: device numbers above come from the kneading mode; this is what recipes using kneading_solid_dough programmed

structure: Cold butter in pieces; knead briefly so the dough stays short (official: kneading program for 45 s or 120 s, or 20 s at speed 4-6).
notes: Official recipes use the kneading program or a short manual step; member recipes use kneading_solid_dough or kneading_soft_dough.

techniques.label: Melt chocolate or butter
structure: Text step before: break the chocolate or cut the butter into pieces (pieces are named in 38 % of the text before official melting steps).
Chocolate at 50 °C (top setting 50 °C for 90 s at speed 1); butter tolerates up to 100 °C.

techniques.label: Warm or heat a liquid or a finished dish

device.reverse: true when the dish contains pieces that must stay whole

structure: Official recipes heat milk at 100 °C (32 of 48 official heated manual steps on milk without egg or starch, 3 at 95 °C); stir at speed 1-2 and keep foaming contents below the foaming limit.
notes: Mostly a member-recipe label (23 official steps); official recipes fold warming into simmer steps.

techniques.label: Sauté onions, garlic or vegetables in fat (anschwitzen, andünsten)

alternatives.note: Manual mode when the food must stay pale or liquid is already in the bowl; reverse when diced vegetables must keep their shape (52.6 % of official manual sauté steps).

structure: Official recipes sauté chopped onion with the roasting program in about three of four cases (213 of 290 first heated steps after chopping onion or garlic); the roasting program stirs on its own and takes no speed.
Text step before: add the fat (oil is named in 37 %) and push the chopped onions down with the spatula (the spatula is named in 50 % of the text before official sauté steps).
Measuring cup out so the steam escapes (state at manual steps of 105-130 °C: removed 148, inserted 67).
Spices bloom at the end of this step; deglaze afterwards with liquid in a scale step.

evidence.selection: technique "anschwitzen", plus roasting steps right after chopping onion, shallot, garlic or ginger

techniques.label: Sear or brown with the roasting program (anbraten)
structure: Measuring cup out before roasting (state at roasting steps: removed 493, inserted 15).
Text step before: add the fat (oil is named in 47 %) and push down with the spatula (52 %).
Roasting time does not scale with mass (fit 225 + 0.125 * grams, R² 0.09); 130 °C for 240 s is the median, 420 s the top setting.
Followed by deglazing and simmering at 100 °C with reverse (66 transitions from roasting to a reverse simmer).
notes: The roasting program stores no speed; the device stirs on its own.

techniques.label: Toast nuts, seeds, spices or flour without fat

device.reverse: true when whole nuts or seeds must stay whole

structure: Measuring cup out; transfer right afterwards so nothing burns in the hot bowl.

techniques.label: Bring a liquid to the boil

timeSeconds.formulaNote: the step must at least cover the physical heat-up time; see timing-model.json

device.reverse: true when the liquid contains pieces that must stay whole

structure: Official recipes never title a step this way (0 official steps); they program a 100 °C simmer step long enough to reach the boil.

techniques.label: Simmer or cook in liquid (soups, stews, sauces, vegetables)

timeSeconds.formulaNote: 100 °C fit over all steps (R² 0.07, residual p10/p90 -526/+623 s); the cooking goal sets the time, the mass only the lower bound

device.reverse: true when pieces must stay whole (vegetable chunks, meat, legumes); false for liquids that are puréed afterwards

structure: Text step before: the liquid goes in by a scale step (stock, water); name what cooks.
The first heated step after filling must at least cover the heat-up time (official headroom: time/tMin median 2.30, p10 0.87).
Long simmering is often split into two steps at the same temperature: 600 s then 300 s at 100 °C (296 transitions).

evidence.selection: technique "koecheln_garen" without the basket as splash guard

techniques.label: Reduce or cook hard with the cooking basket on the lid as splash guard

device.reverse: true when pieces must stay whole

structure: Text step before: remove the measuring cup and set the cooking basket on the lid as a splash guard (98 such text steps; the next step is the working step in 91 %).
This is not steaming: the basket only stops splashes while water evaporates.
For a reduction keep the measuring cup out and extend the simmering time by the seconds given here; do not estimate the evaporation loss. Do not reduce soups.

evidence.selection: text before the step places the cooking basket on the lid ("Kocheinsatz als Spritzschutz")

techniques.label: Thicken or bind: roux, béchamel, custard, starch-bound sauces

device.reverse: false for smooth sauces; true when the sauce already holds pieces

structure: Starch thickens only at 95 °C or more for at least 2 minutes (bridge sanity rule).
Add thickeners in the last 2-3 minutes (SmartRecipe rule) or stir them cold into the liquid first.
Egg-yolk mixtures (custard, sabayon, egg liqueur) at 70-80 °C, speed 2-4, and 70 °C when alcohol is in the bowl (official heated egg-yolk steps: 70 °C in 9 of 25); milk and cream up to 100 °C.
notes: The temperature range starts at 95 °C because starch binds only near the boil; the corpus p10 is 90 °C.

techniques.label: Cook risotto or another rice dish in the bowl
structure: Always reverse rotation at speed 1 so the grains stay whole (reverse in 90.6 % of official steps).
Sauté the rice briefly first, then add the liquid in a scale step.
For plain rice the cooking basket in the bowl is the usual route, see cook_in_basket.

techniques.label: Cook pasta in the bowl (one-pot)
structure: Reverse rotation at speed 1 (reverse in 92.3 % of official steps); the time follows the package cooking time plus about 2 minutes for the heat-up.
Pasta cooks in the sauce or with enough liquid to cover it; keep the total below 3000 g.

techniques.label: Cook milk rice, pudding or porridge

device.reverse: true for milk rice so the grains stay whole; false for smooth pudding

structure: Milk rice and pudding at 90-100 °C (official recipes heat milk at 100 °C); long milk rice steps run with reverse, and foaming contents stay below the foaming limit.

techniques.label: Cook jam, jelly or compote
structure: Measuring cup out and the cooking basket on the lid as splash guard (the basket is named before 20 % of official jam steps).
Jam boils hard: at most 2500 g in the bowl (fill rule for foaming contents).
Add a gelling test as a text step after the cooking step.

techniques.label: Cook potatoes, rice or eggs in the cooking basket

alternatives.note: steaming program for 900 s when the basket only steams above the water.

structure: Text step before: insert the cooking basket and fill it ("Kocheinsatz einsetzen", named before 90 % of these steps); water or stock goes into the bowl in a scale step.
The basket holds about 1000-1200 g of food (SmartRecipe rule).
Often combined with the steamer on top: the basket cooks a side while the steamer cooks the main item.

techniques.label: Steam in the steamer attachment (vegetables, fish, meat, dumplings)
structure: Scale step before: water or stock into the bowl, typically 1000 g, never below 500 g (p10 500 g over 270 steaming steps).

Text steps before: spread the food in the steamer ("im Dampfgaraufsatz verteilen", 376 text steps) and set it on ("Dampfgaraufsatz aufsetzen", 342); name the level (deep bowl or flat insert) before 78.3 % of steaming steps.
Steaming time does not scale with food mass (fit 877 + 0.343 * grams, R² 0.06); pick it by load class (timeByLoadClass).
In 48 % of steaming steps something else cooks in the bowl below; count its mass toward the bowl limit.
notes: Official recipes also steam in manual mode at 120 °C, speed 1, with the steamer fitted (official top settings 120 °C for 180 s or 300 s).

timeSeconds follows timing-model.json (steaming.timeAll over all 309 steaming-program steps). The 207 official steaming steps assigned to this technique give 1080 s (480-3300 s); the difference comes from the sample, not from the device.

techniques.label: Cook sous-vide in the bowl
structure: Text step before: vacuum-sealed food into the basket, water into the bowl to cover it; refill water during long programs (31 text steps say so).
notes: Only 7 steps in the corpus; the device limits come from SmartRecipe.

techniques.label: Slow cook a stew or braise
structure: Sear in a roasting step first, then deglaze, then slow cook (official: 90 °C for 3-4 h).

techniques.label: Ferment or proof (yogurt, dough rising in the bowl)
structure: Official recipes ferment at 40 °C for 1-12 h, member recipes at 37 °C. Yeast doughs usually rise outside the machine instead.

techniques.label: Cook eggs with the egg program
structure: The eggs go into the cooking basket; the program sets time and temperature from size and texture.
notes: Only 3 steps in the corpus, all size medium.

techniques.label: Slice or grate with the food processor attachment
structure: Needs the optional food processor attachment; use it only when the installation says the user owns one (SmartRecipe flag MC_HAS_FOOD_PROCESSOR).

techniques.label: Pre-clean the bowl between stages
structure: Official recipes write a text step instead ("Mixbehälter ausspülen", 731 text steps); prefer the text step.
